closed.Subject: Missing Movement Record and User ID in Task 14039682
closed.subject: Missing Movement Record and User ID in Task 14039682
closed.Description:
Hi GO Support,

We have identified an issue involving a missing movement record from GO and a COMPLETED message that failed to process due to a missing user ID.

Task ID: 14039682
Task Type: GO_STO

Summary
The GO_PUT task was completed; however, RH did not receive the full set of expected movement records. Additionally, the COMPLETED message sent to RH could not be processed because the user ID was missing from the payload.

Impact
There is currently no automated detection or alerting for this issue. The team only becomes aware of the problem after it is reported by a user, at which point manual intervention in BY is required to correct the affected task.

Request
Please investigate the following:

  *
Why the GO_STGFULL movement record was not sent by GO.
  *
Why the resent GO_STGCUB message contained the user ID `tac`.
  *
Why the COMPLETED payload was sent without a user ID.

Issue 1: Missing GO_STGFULL Movement Record
Actual:
The user dropped the item into the cubby. When the MSU arrived, the user selected Bring Bigger for the front location and Warehouse Full for the back location. The task status is now Completed; however, RH only received the GO_STGCUB movement record and did not receive the GO_STGFULL movement record.

Expected:
RH should receive both movement records, GO_STGCUB and GO_STGFULL, with the correct user ID and complete transaction details.

Issue 2: GO_STGCUB Resent with User ID `tac`
Actual:
After identifying the missing user ID, GO resent the GO_STGCUB message; however, the resent message contained the user ID `tac`.

Expected:
The movement message should contain the correct user ID associated with the original user action.

Issue 3: Missing User ID in COMPLETED Payload
Actual:
RH received the COMPLETED message, but processing failed because the user ID field was missing from the payload.

Expected:
The COMPLETED message should include all required fields, including the user ID, to ensure successful processing by RH.

closed.Subject: More than 30 Robots Offline
closed.subject: More than 30 Robots Offline
closed.Description:
Hello! Following up on the previous ticket 00266546 (closed without a conclusive resolution) regarding the event in which 30 robots went offline simultaneously at the SP15 warehouse.

In the last response, the GreyOrange team informed us that the EMQX logs for the requested timeframe could not be retrieved due to Logstash entering an infinite retry loop while attempting to push an oversized payload, which caused it to stop accepting new incoming data. It was also mentioned that the issue had been escalated with the highest priority to the relevant internal team, with the goal of implementing alerts to detect similar log-saving failures early.

Since the ticket was closed without further clarification, we are formally requesting continued follow-up, with objective answers to the points below:

1. What is the current status of the escalation mentioned, and which internal GreyOrange team is responsible for it?
2. Has the root cause of the oversized payload that triggered the Logstash retry loop been identified? What caused this payload to fall outside normal parameters?
3. What concrete changes have already been implemented (or are in progress) in the logging infrastructure (Logstash/EMQX) to prevent an ingestion failure from blocking log recording again?
4. Have the early-detection alerts mentioned already been implemented? If so, since when are they active, and which components do they cover (Logstash, EMQX, GCP push pipeline)?
5. Is there an estimated timeline (ETA) for completing these corrective actions, if still in progress?

We would like to emphasize that the absence of the logs from the original event prevents a complete analysis of the root cause behind the simultaneous shutdown of the 30 robots, which is critical to preventing recurrence. We request a detailed, written response before this ticket is closed.

We look forward to your reply.

Best regards!

closed.Subject: Issues with the ROBOSHOP version and time Config.
closed.subject: Issues with the ROBOSHOP version and time Config.
closed.Description:
Dear Team,

I am writing to report a configuration issue on RoboShop that is impacting
both local maintenance operations and remote troubleshooting.

We are currently unable to change the device time on the RoboShop, and it
is not displaying our local time. Instead, the timestamps are skewed—for
example, showing an incorrect time zone offset (-1100) relative to our
local logs. This discrepancy is directly causing issues when trying to
download and analyze logs both on-site and for the remote teams, as it
makes accurate timestamp matching impossible.

Additionally, we require a stable RoboShop version for the ops laptop. The
current version we are using (2.5.16.0) is not stable and crashes
frequently, particularly when editing maps or clearing errors. We need
either a stable lower version or the latest version file to install on the
Linux laptop. Please share the installation file.

Best regards,

Shabariraj Siddeswaran

closed.Subject: BBBRSP15 – High Rack Turnover Times at Workstations Impacting Operations
closed.subject: BBBRSP15 – High Rack Turnover Times at Workstations Impacting Operations
closed.Description:
Hello GreyOrange Team,
We are observing elevated rack turnover times at BRSP15 after the rack reaches the station and the movement transitions from  Transport Complete - Send Release - Rack start Moving out the stations
For today’s data, we identified:
- 5,971 movements with both events paired.
- 260 cases above 20 seconds (4.35%).
- 80 cases above 1 minute (1.34%).
- The maximum observed delay was 1,262 seconds.

We reviewed representative cases through wrapper logs and safety-state events. The robot completes the available station-side commands, safety restrictions are cleared, and the safety zone is reported as safe. No critical wrapper errors, persistent disconnections, or timeouts were observed.
However, the robot remains connected and continues publishing status updates—such as stateSendCron, one example observed in the wrapper logs—without receiving a new RCS navigation or exit instruction for several minutes. In the analyzed cases, this wait accounts for approximately 5 to 10 minutes before a new movement command is issued.

Could you please help us understand:
1. Why an eligible robot, with safety conditions cleared, does not receive the next exit/navigation instruction from RCS?
2. What condition causes the robot to remain in a status-reporting pattern, such as stateSendCron or another equivalent state, without movement progression?
3. Whether an RCS scheduling, traffic-control, station-handshake, or queue condition could explain this delay?


This behavior is impacting operational throughput because the current rack remains at the station longer than expected, delaying robot departure and the arrival of the next rack.

We will attach some example movement-delay report, representative timelines, wrapper logs to support the investigation.
We need a prompt response and clear actionable next steps, as this issue is currently impacting our operation. This report covers BRSP15 only; however, the same behavior may be occurring at additional warehouses and requir...

closed.Subject: High latency observed in GreyOrange event processing – MXCD13
closed.subject: High latency observed in GreyOrange event processing – MXCD13
closed.Description:
Hello GreyOrange team,
We observed intermittent high processing latency for GreyOrange events at warehouse MXCD13 in Datadog.
During the monitored four-hour window (Datadog timezone: UTC-05:00), the highest observed latencies were:
Event type	Average latency	Maximum latency
transport_api.status	21.46 s	94.5 s
transport.updated	8.92 s	75.6 s
transport.complete	1.98 s	36.7 s
rack.updated.batch	1.21 s	21.6 s
bot.updated.batch	0.57 s	7.3 s


Notable latency spikes include:
- transport.updated: 1 minute 10 seconds around 14:52.
- transport_api.status: 1 minute 34 seconds around 15:46.
- transport_api.status: 1 minute 15 seconds around 16:xx.
- Additional intermittent spikes were observed throughout the monitoring window.
Additionally, we identified the following examples where the time between NEXT_IN_LINE and DELIVERED was 60 seconds or more:
Task	Bot	Rack	Next in line	Delivered	Delta
01M1J20D74MWY2PZ6Y4EFQNZ8H	6	RB-3-00981	15:58:46	16:02:25	219 s
01M1J09FFXFM4QVE6JA9QMZ0KZ	17	RB-3-00022	15:29:23	15:31:21	118 s
01M1J20D74MWY2PZ6Y4KS6EG48	80	RB-3-00016	16:02:56	16:04:51	115 s


We will upload a file containing all TRs processed during the day for reference. Please note that this file represents the complete set of processed TRs and does not independently identify the TRs affected by elevated event latency.
Could you please investigate:
1. Whether there were processing delays, queue buildup, retries, or downstream dependency issues affecting these event types.
2. Whether the observed NEXT_IN_LINE to DELIVERED delays correlate with GreyOrange processing delays or operational conditions at MXCD13.
3. Whether the latency spikes correlate with any degradation, deployment, or operational activity in the MXCD13 environment.
4. The root cause and mitigation actions to prevent recurrence.
Thank you.

Hi Parul,

Our PBT strategy for the peak is different from the non-peak times. Therefore, we plan PBT strategy depending on the volume expected.
To give the best chance for GO to perform , we release orders regularly and the PBTs are set as soon as they are released.

However, forecasted volume and the actual volume does not match.

closed.Subject: Charger Alignment / Charging Failure – Support Required
closed.subject: Charger Alignment / Charging Failure – Support Required
closed.Description:
Hi Team,

We are observing an intermittent charging/alignment issue with the
reflector-based charging system at the Casey site.

During charger validation, the bot initially aligns correctly with the
charger. However, in some cases, the telescopic charging mechanism is
aligning toward the edge of the bot instead of the center charging point,
resulting in charging failures.

We have already performed alignment and validation on multiple bots and
chargers. After the initial adjustment, the alignment looked correct, but
during further observation, we noticed the alignment shifting toward the
edge again.

Troubleshooting done:

   -

   Checked the bot-to-charger alignment.
   -

   Adjusted and validated the reflector-based charger alignment.
   -

   Confirmed the telescopic mechanism was centered after adjustment.
   -

   Continued monitoring during subsequent charging attempts.
   -

   Observed the alignment shifting toward the edge again in some cases.

Please help us investigate this issue and identify the root cause of the
charging/alignment failure.

Thanks,
Shabariraj Siddeswaran

closed.Subject: Multiple Transport Requests missed SLA due to different execution issues
closed.subject: Multiple Transport Requests missed SLA due to different execution issues
closed.Description:
Summary

We identified several Transport Requests that were not executed within the expected SLA. The affected requests belong to OUTBOUND / SALES and are marked as NO CUMPLE in the attached data.

The cases are not all caused by the same reason. We found at least three different scenarios:

Case 1 — Planned tasks without robot assignment

Some Transport Requests were created and planned in GreyOrange, but no robot was assigned and the task never progressed to delivery or completion.

Examples:

Warehouse: BRSP04
Racks: RB-3-06063, RB-3-04901
Workstations: WKS-3-02-003, WKS-3-02-001
Task Status: null
Robot Assigned At: null
Task Delivered At: null
Task Finish At: null

Issue:
The tasks were planned, but they remained stuck before robot assignment. WES can detect this because the task has TASK_CREATED_AT and TASK_PLANNED_AT, but no ROBOT_ASSIGNED_AT, TASK_DELIVERED_AT, or TASK_FINISH_AT.

Request to GreyOrange:
Please confirm why these planned tasks did not receive a robot assignment and why no failure/blocking status was returned.

Case 2 — Rack RB-3-04974 blocked by “No IO point available for rack”

For rack RB-3-04974, the rack status showed the following error:

“unknown reason for busy rack, grep: No IO point available for rack”

Affected data:

Warehouse: BRSP04
Rack: RB-3-04974
Workstation: WKS-3-02-001
Movement Task ID: 01KVDR6E6YRGSNVB5XKWD1PP26
Task Type: picktask
Ranger ID: null
Robot Assigned At: null
Task Delivered At: null
Task Finish At: null

Issue:
Although the rack appeared as available, GreyOrange marked it as busy because there was no IO point available for the rack. This prevented the task from moving forward to robot assignment and execution.

How WES identifies it:
WES sees that the task was created and planned, but no robot was assigned. The blocking reason is only visible in the GreyOrange rack status: “No IO point available for rack.”

Expected recovery action:
Validate IO point availability/configuration for WKS-3-02-001, release or clear t...
